hints: Compare both student values $2.33\text{ V}$ and $2.344\text{ V}$ with the accepted true value $2.321\text{ V}$ by finding the size of each difference.
Recall that accuracy means closeness to the true value, while precision here is shown by the smallest place quoted - $0.01\text{ V}$ versus $0.001\text{ V}$.
Work out $|2.33-2.321|$ and $|2.344-2.321|$ in $\text{V}$ and count decimal places in $2.33\text{ V}$ compared with $2.344\text{ V}$ to judge accuracy and precision separately.
walkthrough: Take the high-quality measurement $2.321\text{ V}$ as the true value to judge accuracy.
State the rule: accuracy is closeness to the true value, precision is the fineness of the quoted reading, shown here by decimal places.
Check accuracy by subtraction: $|2.33-2.321| = 0.009\text{ V}$ and $|2.344-2.321| = 0.023\text{ V}$.
Since $0.009\text{ V} < 0.023\text{ V}$, $2.33\text{ V}$ is closer to the true value and so is more accurate.
Check precision: $2.33\text{ V}$ is given to two decimal places and $2.344\text{ V}$ to three decimal places, so $2.344\text{ V}$ has the finer resolution.
Therefore $2.33\text{ V}$ is more accurate but less precise than $2.344\text{ V}$. This is option C.

options.A: $2.33\text{ V}$ is closer to the true $2.321\text{ V}$ than $2.344\text{ V}$, so it is more accurate, not less accurate.
options.B: $2.33\text{ V}$ is more accurate, and with only two decimal places it is less precise than three-decimal-place $2.344\text{ V}$.
options.C: $2.33\text{ V}$ differs by only $0.009\text{ V}$ from $2.321\text{ V}$ but is quoted to fewer decimal places than $2.344\text{ V}$.
options.D: $2.33\text{ V}$ is more accurate but, quoted to $0.01\text{ V}$ rather than $0.001\text{ V}$, it is less precise than $2.344\text{ V}$.
